Definition: from a shorter form of G2564; an invitation (figuratively):--calling.
KeyPassages: Romans 11:29; 1 Corinthians 1:26; Ephesians 1:18; Philippians 3:14; 2 Thessalonians 1:11; 2 Timothy 1:9
BiblicalUsage: Klesis is the calling, the invitation of God. Romans 11:29 says the gifts and calling of God are without repentance, 1 Corinthians 1:26 says, ye see your calling, brethren, how that not many wise men after the flesh are called, Ephesians 1:18 prays that we may know the hope of his calling, Philippians 3:14 presses toward the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus, 2 Thessalonians 1:11 prays that God would count us worthy of this calling, and 2 Timothy 1:9 says He called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the calling is without repentance because God does not take back His invitations: He calls the foolish, He calls the weak, and He calls them holy. I hold that the high calling of Philippians 3:14 is the prize itself, and the race is worth running because the caller is God.
RelatedBooks: Romans; 1 Corinthians; Ephesians; Philippians; 2 Thessalonians; 2 Timothy
